explanation_en: This means 'to become clear' or 'to be made obvious.' It functions as a passive-like construction where 'quedar' acts as a copular verb indicating a state resulting from an action or process. It is extremely common in both spoken and written Spanish, often followed by 'que' and an indicative clause.

examples.en_text: After the meeting, it became clear to us who was going to lead the project.
examples.target_text: Después de la reunión, nos quedó claro quién iba a liderar el proyecto.

examples.en_text: Yesterday we had an argument, but today it became clear that it was all a misunderstanding.
examples.target_text: Ayer tuvimos una discusión, pero hoy ya quedó claro que todo fue un malentendido.

examples.en_text: Did it become clear to you what you have to do before I leave?
examples.target_text: ¿Te quedó claro lo que tienes que hacer antes de que me vaya?

examples.en_text: With such a simple explanation, the problem became clear to everyone.
examples.target_text: Con esa explicación tan sencilla, a todos les quedó claro el problema.

examples.en_text: I hope it has become clear that I will not tolerate any more lies.
examples.target_text: Espero que haya quedado claro que no toleraré más mentiras.

examples.en_text: Upon reading the contract, it became clear to me that the conditions were not good.
examples.target_text: Al leer el contrato, me quedó claro que las condiciones no eran buenas.

explanation_en: This phrase translates to 'after all,' 'at the end of the day,' or 'when all is said and done.' It is used to introduce a concluding argument or a fundamental truth that supports a previous statement. It is a very common transition phrase in both formal essays and informal speech, helping to synthesize a point.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about what others say; after all, it's your life.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes por lo que digan los demás; al fin y al cabo, es tu vida.

examples.en_text: We decided to buy the used car; after all, we only need it to go to work.
examples.target_text: Decidimos comprar el coche usado; al fin y al cabo, solo lo necesitamos para ir al trabajo.

examples.en_text: You should forgive your brother; after all, he is family.
examples.target_text: Deberías perdonar a tu hermano; al fin y al cabo, es de la familia.

examples.en_text: It doesn't matter if we don't win the prize; after all, the important thing is that we learned a lot.
examples.target_text: No importa si no ganamos el premio; al fin y al cabo, lo importante es que aprendimos mucho.

examples.en_text: After all, it wasn't a bad idea to stay home today with this rain.
examples.target_text: Al fin y al cabo, no fue mala idea quedarnos en casa hoy con esta lluvia.

examples.en_text: Take your time to decide; after all, we are in no hurry.
examples.target_text: Tómate tu tiempo para decidir; al fin y al cabo, no tenemos ninguna prisa.

idiom: se ha cobrado las vidas de
explanation_en: A highly idiomatic and journalistic way to say 'to claim the life of' or 'to take the life of' (referring to disasters, diseases, wars, or accidents). The verb 'cobrarse' is used pronominally here, meaning to collect or demand as a toll. It is a collocated phrase that advanced learners must recognize in news and formal reports.

examples.en_text: The terrible earthquake last week has claimed the lives of more than a hundred people.
examples.target_text: El terrible terremoto de la semana pasada se ha cobrado las vidas de más de cien personas.

examples.en_text: Unfortunately, the traffic accident on the highway claimed the lives of three young people.
examples.target_text: Lamentablemente, el accidente de tráfico en la autopista se cobró las vidas de tres jóvenes.

examples.en_text: This harsh illness has claimed the lives of many elderly people in the region this year.
examples.target_text: Esta dura enfermedad se ha cobrado las vidas de muchos ancianos en la región este año.

examples.en_text: The tropical storm has already claimed the lives of several people on the coast.
examples.target_text: La tormenta tropical ya se ha cobrado las vidas de varias personas en la costa.

examples.en_text: The massive forest fire claimed the lives of two firefighters who were trying to put it out.
examples.target_text: El gran incendio forestal se cobró las vidas de dos bomberos que intentaban apagarlo.

examples.en_text: This long armed conflict has claimed the lives of thousands of innocent civilians.
examples.target_text: Este largo conflicto armado se ha cobrado las vidas de miles de civiles inocentes.

explanation_en: This collocation is widely used in financial and economic contexts to describe a sudden, significant drop in prices, stocks, or indices. While 'caer' means to fall, adding 'con fuerza' emphasizes the intensity and speed of the decline, making it sound much more natural than 'caer mucho'.

examples.en_text: The rain fell heavily throughout the afternoon, flooding some downtown streets.
examples.target_text: La lluvia cayó con fuerza durante toda la tarde, inundando algunas calles del centro.

examples.en_text: The company's stock price fell sharply after the quarterly report.
examples.target_text: El precio de las acciones de la compañía cayó con fuerza tras el informe trimestral.

examples.en_text: The temperature dropped sharply at sunset and we had to turn on the heating.
examples.target_text: La temperatura cayó con fuerza al atardecer y tuvimos que encender la calefacción.

examples.en_text: New car sales fell sharply last month due to the crisis.
examples.target_text: Las ventas de coches nuevos cayeron con fuerza el mes pasado debido a la crisis.

examples.en_text: The cyclist lost control on the curve and fell hard against the ground.
examples.target_text: El ciclista perdió el control en la curva y cayó con fuerza contra el suelo.

examples.en_text: The value of the local currency fell sharply against the dollar this week.
examples.target_text: El valor de la moneda local cayó con fuerza frente al dólar esta semana.

explanation_en: 'Dar impulso' (literally 'to give impulse') means to stimulate, boost, or provide momentum to something. It is a very common business and economic term used when a positive factor drives growth or activity in a market, project, or economy.

examples.en_text: The new tourism law boosted the local economy this summer.
examples.target_text: La nueva ley de turismo dio impulso a la economía local este verano.

examples.en_text: The director's speech boosted our motivation to finish the project on time.
examples.target_text: El discurso de la directora nos dio impulso para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.

examples.en_text: The government investment boosted the development of new technologies.
examples.target_text: La inversión del gobierno dio impulso al desarrollo de nuevas tecnologías.

examples.en_text: Winning the first game of the season boosted the team.
examples.target_text: Ganar el primer partido de la temporada le dio impulso al equipo.

examples.en_text: The book fair boosted reading among the city's youth.
examples.target_text: La feria del libro dio impulso a la lectura entre los jóvenes de la ciudad.

examples.en_text: The social media advertising campaign boosted the company's sales.
examples.target_text: La campaña de publicidad en redes sociales dio impulso a las ventas de la empresa.

explanation_en: This is a standard financial expression used when stock markets or shares finish the trading day at a higher price than the previous close. It uses the prepositional phrase 'al alza' (on the rise). Its opposite is 'cerrar a la baja'.

examples.en_text: The Madrid stock exchange closed higher today thanks to the banks' good results.
examples.target_text: La bolsa de Madrid cerró al alza hoy gracias a los buenos resultados de los bancos.

examples.en_text: The price of oil closed higher this week due to the lack of supply.
examples.target_text: El precio del petróleo cerró al alza esta semana debido a la falta de suministro.

examples.en_text: The technology company's shares closed higher after the announcement of the new product.
examples.target_text: Las acciones de la empresa de tecnología cerraron al alza tras el anuncio del nuevo producto.

examples.en_text: Despite the crisis, the euro closed higher against the dollar in the last session.
examples.target_text: A pesar de la crisis, el euro cerró al alza frente al dólar en la última jornada.

examples.en_text: The coffee market closed higher for the second consecutive day.
examples.target_text: El mercado del café cerró al alza por segundo día consecutivo.

examples.en_text: Almost all sectors of the economy closed higher at the end of the quarter.
examples.target_text: Casi todos los sectores de la economía cerraron al alza al final del trimestre.

explanation_en: 'De cara a' is a highly versatile prepositional phrase meaning 'facing', 'in front of', or 'with a view to / in preparation for'. In this context, 'de cara al público' means directed toward or in front of the public. It is very common in political and professional discourse.

examples.en_text: We have to save money with a view to next year's budget.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que ahorrar dinero de cara al presupuesto del próximo año.

examples.en_text: She is studying hard with a view to the final exams in May.
examples.target_text: Ella está estudiando mucho de cara a los exámenes finales de mayo.

examples.en_text: The team is training hard with a view to Sunday's match.
examples.target_text: El equipo se está entrenando duro de cara al partido del domingo.

examples.en_text: It is important to learn languages with a view to your professional future.
examples.target_text: Es importante aprender idiomas de cara a tu futuro profesional.

examples.en_text: The government is preparing new measures with a view to the upcoming elections.
examples.target_text: El gobierno está preparando nuevas medidas de cara a las próximas elecciones.

examples.en_text: We are making renovations in the house with a view to the winter.
examples.target_text: Estamos haciendo reformas en la casa de cara al invierno.

explanation_en: A very common B2/C1 level verbal periphrasis meaning to execute, conduct, or complete a task or action. It is more formal than 'hacer' or 'realizar' and is heavily used in news, business, and academic writing.

examples.en_text: The engineers have carried out the project very successfully.
examples.target_text: Los ingenieros han llevado a cabo el proyecto con mucho éxito.

examples.en_text: The scientists have carried out several experiments to test the theory.
examples.target_text: Los científicos han llevado a cabo varios experimentos para probar la teoría.

examples.en_text: The authorities have carried out a deep investigation into the accident.
examples.target_text: Las autoridades han llevado a cabo una investigación profunda sobre el accidente.

examples.en_text: The students have carried out a campaign to clean up the school park.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes han llevado a cabo una campaña para limpiar el parque de la escuela.

examples.en_text: The doctors have carried out the surgery without any complications.
examples.target_text: Los médicos han llevado a cabo la operación sin ninguna complicación.

examples.en_text: The directors have carried out important reforms in the company this year.
examples.target_text: Los directores han llevado a cabo importantes reformas en la empresa este año.

explanation_en: This expression means to intervene to help someone or something out of a difficult situation. While it can be used literally, it is very frequently used in financial and political journalism to describe bailouts or economic interventions. 'Acudir' adds a sense of promptness or response to a call.

examples.en_text: When my car broke down before the trip, my brother came to the rescue and lent me his.
examples.target_text: Cuando se me rompió el coche antes del viaje, mi hermano acudió al rescate y me prestó el suyo.

examples.en_text: I didn't know how to finish the report on time, but luckily technology comes to the rescue with these new tools.
examples.target_text: No sabía cómo terminar el informe a tiempo, pero por suerte la tecnología acude al rescate con estas nuevas herramientas.

examples.en_text: If dinner burns, the food delivery service always comes to the rescue.
examples.target_text: Si la cena se quema, el servicio de comida a domicilio siempre acude al rescate.

examples.en_text: I ran out of money halfway through the month, but my parents came to the rescue.
examples.target_text: Me quedé sin dinero a mitad de mes, pero mis padres acudieron al rescate.

examples.en_text: It started raining heavily and a stranger came to the rescue by sharing his umbrella with me.
examples.target_text: Empezó a llover fuerte y un desconocido acudió al rescate compartiendo su paraguas conmigo.

examples.en_text: When the client started shouting, our boss came to the rescue to calm the situation.
examples.target_text: Cuando el cliente empezó a gritar, nuestra jefa acudió al rescate para calmar la situación.

explanation_en: This is a common parenthetical expression used to express a strong wish that something bad does not happen. It is equivalent to 'God forbid' or 'heaven forbid' in English. While it has religious origins, it is used widely in everyday secular speech to express apprehension about negative possibilities.

examples.en_text: If, God forbid, you have an accident, the health insurance will cover all the expenses.
examples.target_text: Si, Dios no lo permita, tienes un accidente, el seguro médico cubrirá todos los gastos.

examples.en_text: If, God forbid, you lose your job, you can always count on my help.
examples.target_text: Si, Dios no lo permita, pierdes el empleo, siempre puedes contar con mi ayuda.

examples.en_text: We want to travel next month, unless, God forbid, the situation gets worse.
examples.target_text: Queremos viajar el próximo mes, a menos que, Dios no lo permita, la situación empeore.

examples.en_text: God forbid, but if you get sick during the trip, call me immediately.
examples.target_text: Dios no lo permita, pero si te enfermas durante el viaje, llámame de inmediato.

examples.en_text: If, God forbid, the business fails, we will have to look for another plan.
examples.target_text: Si, Dios no lo permita, el negocio fracasa, tendremos que buscar otro plan.

examples.en_text: Keep those documents safe because, God forbid, if you lose them it will be a big problem.
examples.target_text: Guarda bien esos documentos porque, Dios no lo permita, si los pierdes será un gran problema.

explanation_en: This idiom literally refers to putting a period at the end of a text, but figuratively it means to end or conclude an activity, discussion, or phase. It is a very natural way to wrap up presentations, shows, or articles. It is slightly more emphatic than simply saying 'terminar.'

examples.en_text: With this last song, we bring tonight's concert to a close.
examples.target_text: Con esta última canción, ponemos punto y final al concierto de esta noche.

examples.en_text: After ten years of marriage, they decided to bring their relationship to a close in a friendly way.
examples.target_text: Después de diez años de matrimonio, decidieron poner punto y final a su relación de forma amistosa.

examples.en_text: I think we have argued enough, so let's put an end to this discussion.
examples.target_text: Creo que ya hemos discutido bastante, así que pongamos punto y final a esta discusión.

examples.en_text: The company is going to bring this project to a close because it is no longer profitable.
examples.target_text: La empresa va a poner punto y final a este proyecto porque ya no es rentable.

examples.en_text: Today I finally bring my university stage to a close and start looking for a job.
examples.target_text: Hoy por fin pongo punto y final a mi etapa universitaria y empiezo a buscar trabajo.

examples.en_text: Last year we brought our adventure abroad to a close and returned home.
examples.target_text: El año pasado pusimos punto y final a nuestra aventura en el extranjero y volvimos a casa.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase is widely used in financial news to indicate that prices, stocks, or markets are increasing or trending upwards. It is the opposite of 'a la baja' (on the decline). It functions as an adjective or adverb and doesn't change for gender or number.

examples.en_text: The price of renting apartments in the city center continues to rise.
examples.target_text: El precio del alquiler de pisos en el centro de la ciudad sigue al alza.

examples.en_text: Tourism in this region is on the rise thanks to the new promotional campaigns.
examples.target_text: El turismo en esta región está al alza gracias a las nuevas campañas de promoción.

examples.en_text: The latest data show that tech employment is clearly on the rise.
examples.target_text: Los últimos datos muestran que el empleo tecnológico va claramente al alza.

examples.en_text: Temperatures will rise over the weekend, so it will be quite hot.
examples.target_text: Las temperaturas irán al alza durante el fin de semana, así que hará bastante calor.

examples.en_text: The electric car company's shares are trading higher today.
examples.target_text: Las acciones de la empresa de coches eléctricos cotizan hoy al alza.

examples.en_text: Interest in learning languages online has been on the rise for a couple of years.
examples.target_text: El interés por aprender idiomas online está al alza desde hace un par de años.
